mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a high-inflation regime where real rates remain negative.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the GDP decline is accompanied by a simultaneous surge in industrial production.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 20-day returns as investors anticipate margin compression.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or inflation (CPIAUCSL) simultaneously falls below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the decline is offset by a simultaneous surge in consumer spending proxies.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 5-year averages signals a stagflation risk, which increases uncertainty and risk premia, resulting in negative S&P 500 60-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the inflation spike is transitory and quickly reversed.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% signals a broad-based collapse in residential and consumer demand, which reduces corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change < -1% AND HOUST monthly change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or the decline is reversed within one month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% month-over-month for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or wage growth (not measured here) fails to keep pace with productivity.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent FEDFUNDS rate held below 2% for more than 12 months in a low-inflation environment signals an extended accommodative monetary policy, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% AND CPIAUCSL < 3% for 12 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or inflation unexpectedly spikes above 4% during the period.
